title: Relative cyclic restriction model and forgetting the residual action
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups and $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism, where $\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ is the discrete additive group. Put $\tau=u(1)$. Use internal $R$-modules and condensed-group actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ let $\Gamma_J^G:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ be the submodule fixed by $J$ after every profinite base change, retaining the $G$-action. These action categories are Grothendieck abelian and these functors are right adjoint to exact trivial-$J$ inflation, with the invariant-inclusion normalization [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Derive them in the full ordinary action categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restriction along $1_G\times u$ gives a natural transformation of triangulated functors on $D^+$,
$$\beta^G:R\Gamma_H^G\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G D(\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}),$$
whose degree-zero map is the inclusion of invariant submodules. For a bounded-below complex $N^\bullet$ of $G\times\mathbf Z$-modules, let $K^G(N^\bullet)$ be the two-column total of $N^\bullet\xrightarrow{T-1}N^\bullet$, in cyclic degrees $0,1$, where $T$ acts by $1\in\mathbf Z$, with total differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_N$ in cyclic degree $a$. This defines a triangulated functor and has an invariant-normalized natural isomorphism
$$\lambda^G:QK^G(N^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(QN^\bullet).$$
In particular, for a module $N$ put $c_N^G=(\lambda_N^G)^{-1}\beta_N^G:R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])\to Q[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$.

Forgetting the $G$-action is exact and conservative on modules and ordinary derived categories. It identifies the underlying $R\Gamma_J^G(N)$ with $R\Gamma_{R,J}(\operatorname{Res}_J N)$ for $J=H,\mathbf Z$, and takes $\beta^G,\lambda^G,c^G$ to respectively the canonical derived restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], the rank-one isomorphism of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and their composite. These identifications are natural in coefficients and preserve the canonical shifts and triangle boundaries.

For $G=1$ and $N=R$ with trivial $H$-action, let $V^q=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline H^q],R)$ with the inhomogeneous differential, and let $j:QV^\bullet\to\mathscr B_R(H)$ be the canonical underived-to-derived bar augmentation. With $\eta:R\Gamma_{R,H}(R[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B_R(H)$ the invariant-normalized comparison of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar], one has
$$c_R^1\eta^{-1}j=Q(\epsilon),$$
where $\epsilon:V^\bullet\to[R\xrightarrow{0}R]$ is the cochain map given by the identity in degree zero, evaluation at $u(1)$ in degree one, and zero in degrees at least two. No assertion that $\beta^G$ is an isomorphism is made.

None of the preceding constructions requires $\beta^G$ invertible.
